title: Learned Execution Graphs for Anomaly Detection & Drift in APIs — Ritvik Pandya, JP Morgan Chase
talk_summary: Ritvik Pandya describes representing API request processing as a short-lived DAG (execution graph) to baseline normal behavior, then detect anomalies and classify drift (structural, scale, covariate) to localize faults and reduce alert noise. It is a statistical observability/root-cause module for payment APIs, not an agent-orchestration talk.

takeaways.technique: Per-run execution DAG as a baseline artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Each request is modeled as a DAG of nodes/steps; the baseline DAG lets them see which node deviated instead of only an end-to-end latency number.
takeaways.evidence_quote: representing the uh overall request processing as DAG and using tag simplifies most of the things here

takeaways.what_they_do: They flag when a node is added or removed versus baseline as a distinct 'structural drift' class, separate from latency drift.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if any new node or new step added which you are not aware of that could be one of the thing

takeaways.technique: Per-segment baselines instead of global thresholds
takeaways.what_they_do: Baselines are computed per client/request-type rather than one global average, because different segments legitimately differ.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the baseline will change client to client and now you know that uh what your threshold it and uh how you can u reduce the noise

takeaways.technique: Two-tier check: cheap first pass, expensive only on deviation
takeaways.what_they_do: A cheap tier-1 check runs always; deeper analysis only triggers when the baseline is exceeded, saving resources.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If uh everything looks Good. You don't need to go to the tier two uh or next tier of check

takeaways.technique: Synthetic anomaly injection for pre-production training
takeaways.what_they_do: They replay millions of traces over 7 days, inject known anomalies, and train/validate the detector before going live.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for 7 days of the time millions of uh traces were um you know injected or uh in the system then you inject the problem
takeaways.numbers: 7 days of traces, millions of traces

takeaways.what_they_do: Before automating a fix across all nodes, they roll it to 5-10% of machines, verify, then expand.
takeaways.evidence_quote: roll out that system uh um solution for say 5% or 10% of your uh machines monitor it verify everything looks good and then you roll out for your 100%
